text:
As I stand here, surrounded by glass walls and sterile modernism in the first room, I feel a certain weight of anticipation—a quiet invitation to observe, to listen, to wait. The emptiness, almost sacred, makes the mundane profound.

Then, in the second space, the vibrant wall of text and illuminated screens radiate curiosity and excitement. The world of research and development seems to pulse with possibility, sparking questions in my mind about human progress, our desires to know, to create, to connect. It feels invigorating, like witnessing the future in real-time, but also humbling in the face of infinite intellect and knowledge.
